claim.quote: The combination with the corresponding measurement performed with data collected by the CMS experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV leads to an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

date.note: Phys. Lett. B 779 (2018) 283 publication year; arXiv preprint submitted 1 August 2017

name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to tau leptons

significance.quote: an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS was the first single experiment to see the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau leptons, showing that the Higgs couples to this heavy relative of the electron.
summary.technical: 35.9 fb^-1 at 13 TeV gives 4.9 sigma for H -> tau tau; combining with 7 and 8 TeV data gives 5.9 sigma and a signal strength of 1.09 +0.27 -0.26 times the standard model expectation.

title: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons with the CMS detector
why_it_matters: It was the first direct observation of the Higgs boson coupling to fermions by a single experiment, testing whether the Higgs gives mass to matter particles as predicted.
